page.overview:
What is Air Nomad ancient paths?

Originally, flying bison herds used natural air currents high in the sky to speed up their migrations. After bonding with these animals and learning from them, early airbenders also began to use these currents and began to refer to them as "paths". Their use of these air currents to travel in the sky contributed to the naming of the roving airbenders as the "Air Nomads".

The paths were popular and widely used in the era of Sonam, when the Air Nomads were very active across the entire globe. The ancient paths also allowed the Air Nomads to traverse the Endless Ocean, resulting in their discovery of the Immortal Storm and the lion turtle islands. Avatar Sonam used the paths when she traveled to the islands in the Immortal Storm, meeting with the lion turtles there and creating her powerful staff.

By the 1st century BG, the ancient paths had faded from knowledge among the Air Nomads, and Avatar Aang grew up ignorant of them.

Around 110 AG, Aang accidentally freed Tagah, an Air Nomad of the era of Sonam, from his energy prison. Feigning a cooperative spirit, Tagah agreed to guide Aang and his friends to the lion turtle islands to recover Sonam's staff. To do so, he led Zuko's airship into the air currents which formed the Air Nomad ancient paths. In this way, the group quickly covered great distances. As the group traversed the paths, Aang and Tagah bonded as the ancient master introduced the young Avatar to airbending techniques and shared his experiences. The group's journey on the ancient paths came to an end when they reached the Immortal Storm.
